question: Southwest flight 3851 from PHX to SFO on 2026-01-03 pushed back late. How late was the departure, and what did the carrier attribute the delay to?

content.text: I'll look up that flight directly.

input.sql: SELECT * FROM flights WHERE flight_date='2026-01-03' AND flight_number='3851'
SELECT * FROM flights WHERE flight_number='3851' AND origin='PHX'

SELECT r.flight_id, r.origin, r.destination, r.sched_dep_utc, f.dep_delay_minutes, f.arr_delay_minutes, f.delay_carrier, f.delay_nas, f.delay_late_aircraft, f.status FROM rotation_sequence r JOIN flights f USING(flight_id) WHERE r.tail_number='N8633A' AND r.sched_dep_utc >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-01-03 11:00:00+00' ORDER BY r.sched_dep_utc LIMIT 12

content.text:
**2026-01-03|WN|3851|PHX|SFO|0855** (tail N8633A) pushed back 142 minutes late — scheduled 08:55 Phoenix / 15:55Z, off at 11:17 local / 18:17Z — and arrived SFO 141 minutes late (12:26 vs 10:05 local).

The carrier attributed the whole 141 minutes of arrival delay to **national airspace system (NAS)**: delay_nas 141, with carrier, weather, security, and late_aircraft all zero. That is consistent with the aircraft's inbound: the same tail's previous leg, 2026-01-03|WN|3851|MSY|PHX|0540, arrived PHX 11 minutes *early* (15:04Z against a 15:15Z schedule), so this was not an inbound-aircraft cascade — the delay started at PHX. The data does not say which NAS constraint (SFO flow control, ATC, volume) caused it; that would need the BTS cause detail or an ATC advisory log, which is not in this extract.

The delay then propagated down N8633A's rotation for the rest of the day, all of it booked as late_aircraft: WN4106 SFO–PHX 144 late (133 late_aircraft), WN172 PHX–LGB 135 (128), WN65 LGB–LAS 140 (124), WN65 LAS–DAL 144 (116), and WN65 DAL–HOU 155 (114). The tail reset overnight at HOU, departing only 3 minutes late on WN2999 to STL the next morning.
